finding.claim: dotfiles:'deny' is bypassed by the directory-listing fallback: a request for a dot-directory with a trailing slash returns the names (and with jsonFormat extended, sizes and mtimes) of non-dot entries inside it.
finding.source: E1: GET /.git/ (any dot-directory with trailing slash) with opts.list enabled and opts.index unset.

trace.note: wildcard handler calls pumpSendToReply
send called with dotfiles 'deny'; dot path returns 403 (send internals not readable locally)
error case: statusCode 403, options.index unset, pathname ends with '/'
opts.list truthy, so sendDirectoryList is called
sendDirectoryList -> dirList.path
path() resolves the dot-directory; it is inside root, so returned
dirList.send called with dotfiles 'deny'
list filters only names starting with '.' inside the listed directory, not the requested path itself
names or extended stats returned to client

finding.guards_checked: Dotfile check applies only to the names inside the listed dir (lib/dirList.js:83-84). No check that the requested path itself is a dotfile. path() checks only root containment (lib/dirList.js:14-22, 192-199). dotfiles:'ignore' yields 404 and does not reach this branch (index.js:412-413). File bodies remain blocked: /.git/config returns 403 from send.

finding.claim: allowedPath is evaluated only on the requested directory string, not on the index file send resolves and serves, so an app rule that denies an index file by exact match is bypassed via the directory URL.
finding.source: E1: GET /admin/ (or GET /admin, which recurses to /admin/).
finding.sink: send resolves the directory to its index file and returns it as type file, which is served (index.js:296-302, 419-440).

trace.note: allowedPath('/admin/', root, req) called once on the requested string
send resolves trailing-slash dir to index file (send internals not readable locally)
metadata.path (resolved file) is available but not passed to allowedPath
file case serves the resolved index file
for /admin with no slash, recursion with /admin/ repeats the same allowedPath check on the directory string

finding.guards_checked: allowedPath is the only access check and runs before send on the requested string only. Impact depends on the app's allowedPath rule. Case-insensitive filesystems (default on darwin) may add a case-variant bypass if the rule is case-sensitive.
